newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hagemeyer ready to make more acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Hagemeyer ready to make more acquisitions.

text.p: Trading company Hagemeyer NV said on Thursday it was in talks over a possible acquisition, but declined to give details on the candidates.

Hagemeyer chairman Andrew Land said the company was not in discussions about acquisitions in the speciality food sector at this moment, in which the company had previously stated its wished to expand.
"But, we are in talks," he told Reuters. "I'd rather not tell with which kind of businesses."
"One out of ten times we come to a final agreement," he said.
Hagemeyers' trading business also includes consumer and professional products, electrical distribution and automotive and technical products.
The company aims to increase turnover by some 12 to 15 percent annually.
"Organic growth should meet an average of six to seven percent annually and an average of seven to nine percent increase in turnover should come from acquisitions," Land said.
Hagemeyer aims at medium sized to large acquisitions. Land said an acquisition with turnover of some 500 million to one billion guilders would be considered large.
In the electrical distribution business, in which it is one of the three largest players in Europe, Hagemeyer is on the lookout for both medium sized and large acquisitions, Land said.
In the U.S. it was aiming for a large acquisition, he added.
Hagemeyer has said previously that an acquisition in Asia also has high priority.
"But we also want to increase our market share in Europe," Land said.
Land said that Ceteco, in which Hagemeyer holds a 70 percent stake, was focusing on small acquisitions in South America to expand its retail business.
Ceteco has outlets in Peru, Argentina, Honduras, Venezuela, Ecuador, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Mexico.
